newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian trade sees tin at fresh lows, copper steady.
newsitem.headline: Asian trade sees tin at fresh lows, copper steady.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) tin prices are expected to fall to new two-year lows while copper will probably remain steady to higher despite views the market is overbought, Far Ease base metal dealers said on Friday.
"A lot of people feel tin should move further down," a dealer for a European metal trading company said. "The next target is US$5,500. It's pretty weak."
Three-month tin dived on Thursday on the LME to $5,580 a tonne as fund liquidation and selling picked up steam due to a stocks fall and shaky technical signals for the metal.
"I think tin will try a new low this afternoon," another dealer said. "It has nowhere to go but down."
LME brokers Brandeis said tin's poor close on the chart "suggests a test of support at $5,500 and then $5,420".
Tin was indicated by the trade at 0400 GMT at $5,590/610 a tonne against its close on the LME of $5,600.
One trader said the weakness of tin will persist over the short to medium term with nothing on the horizon seen to perk up the market.
Copper prices, on the other hand, were expected to remain steady and keep its upward bias intact.
"Copper should persist in its high cycle and should consolidate at these levels," a dealer said. "Its next target is $2,555 (a tonne)."
"Copper will go higher. I don't see a drop right now," another trader said.
Metal brokers Macquarie said in their daily report that support for the red metal was seen at the lows on Thursday and it closed relatively unchanged.
"For the short-term, we think these levels are maintainable and again we look higher," Macquarie said.
Three-month copper was seen by regional dealers at $2,530/35 a tonne at 0400 GMT, slightly higher than its late quote on the LME of $2,530/31 a tonne.
Copper stocks will probably drop by around 1,000-2,000 tonnes when the LME report is released at 0800 GMT, dealers said.
